name: Ehud
overview: Ehud is a male figure from the tribe of Benjamin, uniquely identified as the son of Bilhan according to 1 Chronicles 7:10. The biblical record provides limited additional details about his life or activities. His mention serves primarily to establish genealogical connections within the tribe of Benjamin.
namesAndTitles: The name Ehud means 'united,' as noted in 1 Chronicles 7:10. This proper name does not appear to have been given by God but reflects a common Hebrew personal name without further theological significance in the text.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly records Ehud as the son of Bilhan (1 Chronicles 7:10). Additionally, inferred relationships suggest that Ehud may be connected as a father to Naaman, Ahijah, and Gera (1 Chronicles 8:7), though these are not directly stated. Beyond these, no other family relationships are documented.
scriptureSignificance: Ehud's primary importance lies in his placement within the genealogical records of the tribe of Benjamin, which helps trace the lineage and tribal identity of Israel. His mention as the son of Bilhan preserves the continuity of Benjaminite heritage. While the biblical text does not elaborate on his personal deeds or role, his inclusion contributes to the broader biblical narrative of God's providential preservation of His chosen people through their families.
